to support the Department Chair and serve as a key administrative partner to departmental leadership. This role provides high-level executive and operational support by managing the Chair's office, coordinating meetings and events, preparing reports and communications, and supporting faculty committees. The incumbent advises the Chair and Chief Administrative Officer (CAO) on policy implementation and departmental initiatives, conducts research and analysis to inform administrative decisions, and serves as a primary liaison with the UCLA Dean's and Chancellor's Offices, faculty, government agencies, and external partners. This position plays a critical role in ensuring the efficient operation of the Chair's office and advancing the department's academic and administrative mission.

Skill to independently research and analyze information, problems, operational practices and procedures to define issues, formulate actions and carry out decisions in a logical and appropriate manner;

Demonstrated ability to handle confidential issues with tact and diplomacy. Excellent oral and written communication skills to establish and maintain cooperative working relationships with faculty, staff, students, deans, chancellors, donors, industry representatives and politicians.
Demonstrated skill in writing effective, clear, logical, and concise correspondence,
Demonstrated ability to work independently and complete projects within specified deadlines.
Demonstrated knowledge of UCLA academic personnel policies and procedures.
Demonstrated knowledge in preparing concise and logical analytic reports.
Demonstrated knowledge of Microsoft Word, Excel, and Powerpoint programs.
Demonstrated knowledge of medical and scientific terminology.
Demonstrated ability to prioritize projects to meet scheduled deadlines.
Ability to work under heavy workload, with changing priorities and constant interruptions.
Ability to analyze information and data from manuscripts, abstracts, and articles for program application.
Ability to manage complex short-term and long-term projects. Ability to maintain the highest confidentiality of critical discussions as they relate to faculty, staff and trainee data.
